title: Groupoïdes de Teichmüller et les S0 Tg,!ν, S0 TG : notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
Setting. The hats denote stable compactifications: \hat M_{0,n} is the Deligne–Mumford–Knudsen space \bar M_{0,n}, \hat{\mathcal X}_{0,n} is the universal stable curve over it, and 'MD' means Mumford–Deligne (stable) curves. The page studies the inclusion M_{0,5} ⊂ \hat M_{0,5} by viewing \hat M_{0,5} through the universal curve over \hat M_{0,4}. This belongs to the 'tour de Teichmüller' programme: it describes the low-dimensional strata (n ≤ 5) in an inductive way.

(1) An intermediate open set. Between M_{0,5} and \hat M_{0,5} sits \hat M'_{0,5}. It consists of the stable 5-pointed genus-0 curves that remain stable after deleting point 5, so no stabilization is needed when point 5 is forgotten. Grothendieck identifies \hat M'_{0,5} ≅ \hat{\mathcal X}^*_{0,4}, an open subset of the universal curve \hat{\mathcal X}_{0,4} → \hat M_{0,4} ≅ P^1. A point of a fibre that is neither marked nor a node gives a stable 5-pointed curve whose 4-pointed reduction is the original fibre.

(2) Explicit model of the universal curve. \hat{\mathcal X}_{0,4} → P^1 × P^1 is the blow-up of the three points of the diagonal Δ over 0, 1, ∞. Over λ ∈ P^1 the trivial family has the four sections 0, 1, ∞ and the diagonal z = λ. At λ = 0, 1, ∞ the diagonal meets a constant section. Blowing up these three points separates the sections and makes the special fibres two-component nodal curves. This is the classical model of \bar M_{0,5} as a degree-5 del Pezzo surface (P^1×P^1 blown up in 3 points, equivalently P^2 blown up in 4 points). The ten boundary curves are:
- the strict transforms of the 3 constant sections and of the diagonal;
- the 3 exceptional curves;
- the strict transforms of the 3 special fibres.

(3) What is removed. \hat{\mathcal X}^*_{0,4} = \hat{\mathcal X}_{0,4} minus the strict transforms \tilde Δ_1, \tilde Δ_2, \tilde Δ_3, \tilde Δ of the four sections.

(4) 'What is missing from \hat M_{0,5} via \hat{\mathcal X}^*_{0,4}?' These are the stable (0,5)-curves that become unstable when a point is removed, i.e. point 5 lies on a component with only three special points. Two cases, matching the two sketches:
- Point 5 is on a tail together with exactly one point i (figure '5* i', 1 ≤ i ≤ 4). These are the four boundary divisors D_{i5}, which correspond to the four sections.
- Point 5 is on the middle component of a three-component chain carrying two points at each end (first figure). There are three such curves, indexed by the pairings of {1,2,3,4}. They correspond to the three nodes of the singular fibres of \hat{\mathcal X}_{0,4}, presumably the 'pts isolés'.
So \hat M_{0,5} = \hat M'_{0,5} ⊔ (4 divisors) ⊔ (3 points). The other sketches (a three-branch comb, a three-component curve with marked points) are pictures of the boundary strata.

(5) Next inductive step, sketched only. The fibre product \hat{\mathcal X}_{0,4} ×_{\hat M_{0,4}} \hat{\mathcal X}_{0,4} → \hat{\mathcal X}_{0,4} ≅ \hat M_{0,5} is considered together with the five distinguished loci σ_i (1 ≤ i ≤ 4) and the diagonal δ. The evident aim is to obtain \hat{\mathcal X}_{0,5} (≅ \hat M_{0,6}) by modifying this fibre product along the sections and diagonal, just as \hat{\mathcal X}_{0,4} came from \hat{\mathcal X}_{0,3} × \hat{\mathcal X}_{0,3} = P^1×P^1 with 3 sections plus diagonal. The base case \hat M_{0,3} = point, \hat{\mathcal X}_{0,3} = P^1 is noted at the bottom. This is exactly the pattern of Keel's later construction of \bar M_{0,n+1} as an iterated blow-up of \bar M_{0,n} ×_{\bar M_{0,n-1}} \bar M_{0,n}. Here it is only indicated, not carried out.
errors: The identification \hat{\mathcal X}^*_{0,4} ≃ \hat{\mathcal X}_{0,4} − (\tilde Δ_1 ∪ \tilde Δ_2 ∪ \tilde Δ_3 ∪ \tilde Δ) as written omits the three nodes of the singular fibres. These must also be removed for the isomorphism with \hat M'_{0,5}. The later mention of 'pts isolés' seems to correct or acknowledge this, so it is a gap in the first statement rather than a real error.
The step to \hat{\mathcal X}_{0,5} via the fibre product is only indicated. No blow-up centres are specified, and the fibre product is singular over the nodes, which would need treatment.

ideas.what: Universal curve over \bar M_{0,4} is isomorphic to \bar M_{0,5}; forgetting point 5 is the universal curve map
ideas.modern_name: Knudsen's forgetful/stabilization morphism \bar M_{g,n+1} ≅ universal curve over \bar M_{g,n}
ideas.usually_credited_to: F. Knudsen (Projectivity of the moduli space of stable curves II, 1983; circulated earlier)
ideas.where_published: Implicit in Esquisse d'un programme's discussion of the Teichmüller tower and boundary of \hat M_{0,n}

ideas.what: \bar M_{0,5} as blow-up of P^1×P^1 at the three diagonal points (0,0), (1,1), (∞,∞)
ideas.usually_credited_to: classical / Kapranov, Keel (early 1990s explicit modular descriptions)

ideas.what: Stratification of \bar M_{0,5} relative to forgetting a point: the open set where forgetting needs no stabilization, plus 4 divisors and 3 points
ideas.modern_name: Stratification of the forgetful map / contraction (stabilization) loci

ideas.what: Inductive construction of the universal curve over \bar M_{0,n+1} from the fibre product of universal curves, with marked sections and diagonal
ideas.modern_name: Keel's blow-up construction of \bar M_{0,n+1} from \bar M_{0,n} ×_{\bar M_{0,n-1}} \bar M_{0,n}

missed.claim: Grothendieck sets up \hat{\mathcal X}_{0,4} ×_{\hat M_{0,4}} \hat{\mathcal X}_{0,4} with the sections σ_i and diagonal δ as the route to the next stage of the tower. This prefigures Keel's (1992) inductive blow-up description of \bar M_{0,n}, about a decade before Keel, in the context of the Teichmüller tower. It remains a sketch.
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: Mostly historical. It documents that Grothendieck was using the iterated-fibre-product/blow-up picture of \bar M_{0,n} in his Teichmüller-tower work around 1978–80. That picture is now central (Keel, Kapranov) for cell structures and Gal(\bar Q/Q) actions on boundary strata.

deep.surprise_reason: The completed content is standard: the blow-up model of \bar M_{0,5}, Knudsen's universal curve, and the stabilization strata. The only mildly notable point is the early sketch of the fibre-product induction anticipating Keel, but it is not developed.
transcription_corrections: Line 1 diagram: \hat M'_{0,5} sits between M_{0,5} and \hat M_{0,5}, with both inclusions drawn; it is ≅ \hat{\mathcal X}^*_{0,4} (the '\wr|' is an isomorphism sign).
'stables en ... le terme 5' likely reads 'stables en enlevant le point 5' (the struck word is crossed out).
'Que manque-t-il : ... \hat M_{0,5} via \hat{\mathcal X}^*_{0,4} ?' likely reads 'Que manque-t-il à \hat M_{0,5} via \hat{\mathcal X}^*_{0,4} ?'.
'stables en enlevant un des pts : l'un au moins ...' is uncertain; the sense is that point 5 lies on a component with only three special points.
'pts isolés — en complexe' is uncertain; it plausibly refers to the 3 isolated points (the nodes) in the complement.
